title: Partner asset adoption and brand voice checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic checklist + living reference for onboarding partner creative assets and marketplace copy while preserving Redwood brand voice and licensing constraints. It is intended for partnerships, PMs, partner eng, and the marketplace ops owner who will shepherd acceptance.

Scope:
- All marketplace publications (AWS, Azure, GCP, vendor storefronts) and co-branded partner microsites.
- Creative assets: logos, screenshots, explainer GIFs, short videos, architecture diagrams, product screenshots, and sample prompts.
- Copy: 1-line tagline, 2-line elevator, long description, feature bullets, trial CTA, support blurb.

Quick acceptance checklist (must pass all):
- Brand & logo: partner provided vector logo (SVG or EPS), background-free PNG (2x) and permission form signed.
- Asset quality: all screenshots >= 1920x1080 or 1280x800 (clearly legible), no internal URLs visible, no PII in samples.
- Copy: short tagline <= 70 chars, long description <= 1200 chars, feature bullets 3–5 lines.
- Technical metadata: billing SKU, region availability, supported models list, latency SLO expectation (if offering Dedicated).
- Legal/licensing: partner grants non-exclusive right to display logo + 90-day reuse window; any third-party model must include model license link.
- Security/compliance flags: if partner claims FedRAMP/HIPAA-readiness, attach supporting attestation docs.
- Translations: English default; localized descriptions for en-GB, de-DE, fr-FR when targeting EU marketplaces.

Creative asset inventory (template for partner intake):
- brand-logo.svg (required)
- brand-mark-white-bg.png (optional)
- screenshot-hero-1.png (required) – annotated: what user sees, where LLM output shows up
- screenshot-ux-2.png (optional) – mobile view
- gif-flow-30s.mp4 (optional) – under 30s, no audio required
- diagram-arch.pdf (optional) – must scrub internal hostnames
- sample-invocation.txt (required) – short prompt + expected output (no real customer data)

Creative licensing matrix (quick rules):
- Partner logo: partner retains ownership; Redwood receives display license for product pages and marketing for duration of listing + 30 days post delist.
- Screenshots/GIFs: partner represents assets are cleared for public use and do not include third-party rights. If partner uses third-party imagery, attach release.
- Video demos: require written consent if partner includes voiceover featuring people (model release).

Copy tone & voice primer (short):
- Voice anchor: technical, developer-first, production-focused. Speak to engineers and platform owners.
- Level: assume reader knows basic LLM concepts; emphasize operational benefits (latency, cost, SLAs) not model hype.
- Tone: concise, factual, no hyperbolic adjectives (avoid words like "best-in-class"). Use measurable statements where possible.
- Example do: "Predictable 99.9% uptime with dedicated GPU pools and burst capacity"
- Example don't: "World-class LLM superpowers at unbeatable prices"

Suggested copy variants (examples to give partners as templates):
- Tagline (70 chars max): "Redwood Inference — predictable LLM serving for production apps"
- 2-line elevator (140 chars max): "Deploy LLM features with consistent latency and cost controls. Hosted API, dedicated pools, and private deployments for regulated workloads."
- Long description (500–900 chars example): "Redwood Inference provides a unified serving platform that helps engineering teams ship LLM features with predictable performance and cost. Choose hosted endpoints for fastest integration, reserved Dedicated capacity for throughput guarantees, or a Private deployment when you need VPC-level isolation. Built-in routing, caching, and automatic fallbacks protect your user experience while reducing token spend. Integrates with KMS and observability hooks for enterprise controls and auditing."
- Feature bullets (short):
  - Hosted API: quick start REST + SDKs, streaming and function calls
  - Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with autoscale and SLAs
  - Private deployment: VPC/on-prem options with audit logs and KMS
  - Cost controls: batching, cache, and quantization recommendations

Marketplace-specific copy constraints (examples):
- AWS Marketplace title limit: 200 chars — prefer 60–80 chars for clarity
- Azure: include supported SKUs & billing cadence explicit in listing
- GCP: list region availability and any additional networking prerequisites

Acceptance gates (detailed):
1) Completeness scan (owner: partner-ops)
   - Are required assets present? (logo, hero image, sample invocation)
   - Are all fields filled in listing form? (billing SKU, contact email, tags)
2) Security & legal check (owner: security-compliance)
   - Any claims about compliance? Attach evidence.
   - Third-party data use? Confirm redaction of customer data.
3) Copy & brand review (owner: marketing)
   - Adheres to brand voice primer? No hyperbole, measurable claims.
   - CTA present (trial or contact sales) and accurate support path.
4) Marketplace vendor QA (owner: marketplace-ops)
   - Listing renders correctly across mobile and desktop.
   - Links (privacy policy, docs, support) are reachable and not behind auth.
5) Final signoff (owner: go-to-market lead)
   - Checklist completed, acceptance stamps from each owner recorded in intake ticket.

Localization & accessibility notes:
- Provide alt text for every image (required).
- For EU launches, include data residency/region copy and translated descriptions for German and French where possible.
- Avoid color-dependent callouts; include clear text labels in screenshots.

Common failure modes (observed in past launches):
- Partner sends low-res screenshots with visible internal hostnames or user emails.
- Copy uses marketing hyperbole that fails Marketplace content policy review.
- Missing billing SKU or contact results in listing delays.

Roadmap items / TODOs (working list):
- [ ] Create Marketplace copy snippets kit (en/DE/FR) for partner self-serve (owner: Diego Ramos)
- [ ] Build Slack intake form to collect assets and auto-create JIRA intake (owner: Product Ops)
- [ ] Document a short legal template for partner display license (owner: Legal)

Notes to self / open questions:
- How strict should we be about screenshots that show partner UI with identifiable customer logos? (ask legal)
- Should we include an optional section for performance benchmarks (p90 latency, cost per token) or reserve that for Dedicated product pages only?

References & helpful links:
- Marketplace asset standards (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GT/marketplace-asset-standards
- Example listing (internal): https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prod-EXAMPLE-1
- Intake ticket template: JIRA-3492

Revision history:
- 2025-08-07 Maya Chen: initial draft
- 2025-08-20 Priya Kapoor: added legal checklist and localization notes
- 2025-09-02 Ethan Brooks: sample copy variants and acceptance gates refined

Unpolished fragments (intentional — keep for collaborators):
- "Notes: partner wants a co-branded webinar tile, need to confirm usage rights"
- "Consider a short "how it integrates" callout for ISVs using Redwood Dedicated"

End of doc.
